scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** labels, help text, attachments, or actions exceed the available inline space
- **THEN** content remains visible, controls remain operable, and the component introduces no horizontal page overflow
scenarios.id: forms/composer::Composer preserves content at bounded narrow widths::Composer is rendered with long content in a narrow container
scenarios.name: Composer is rendered with long content in a narrow container
scenarios.requirement: Composer preserves content at bounded narrow widths
scenarios.requirementContent: Composer SHALL fit its container, permit editing content and supporting copy to wrap, allow the editing region to grow to its documented maximum before consumer-owned overflow behavior applies, and stack supporting regions when their inline layout no longer fits.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a labelled editing surface is placed in the Composer editing-surface region
- **THEN** the Composer supplies layout and visual containment while the consumer retains editor semantics and behavior
scenarios.id: forms/composer::Composer provides structured regions without owning an editor::A consumer mounts its editor
scenarios.name: A consumer mounts its editor
scenarios.requirement: Composer provides structured regions without owning an editor
scenarios.requirementContent: The styles package SHALL support a Composer root with optional label/help, toolbar, editing-surface, attachments, status, and actions regions. The editing-surface region SHALL accept a consumer-provided textarea, contenteditable element, or editor mount point without changing that surface's value or document model.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the consumer applies the editing surface's supported read-only semantics and the documented Composer state hook
- **THEN** the Composer displays the read-only presentation without disabling unrelated actions implicitly
scenarios.id: forms/composer::Composer states remain semantic and externally controlled::Consumer makes the surface read-only
scenarios.name: Consumer makes the surface read-only
scenarios.requirement: Composer states remain semantic and externally controlled
scenarios.requirementContent: Composer SHALL style the root `:focus-within` presentation when a descendant is focused. Composer SHALL visually support invalid, disabled, and read-only presentations only when the consumer supplies the corresponding native or ARIA state on the editing surface and documented state hook on the root. Styling SHALL NOT imply that a nested editor engine has enforced those states.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the editing surface exposes `aria-invalid="true"` and references an error message
- **THEN** the Composer displays its invalid presentation and preserves the programmatic relationship to the message
scenarios.id: forms/composer::Composer states remain semantic and externally controlled::Consumer reports invalid content
scenarios.name: Consumer reports invalid content
scenarios.requirement: Composer states remain semantic and externally controlled
scenarios.requirementContent: Composer SHALL style the root `:focus-within` presentation when a descendant is focused. Composer SHALL visually support invalid, disabled, and read-only presentations only when the consumer supplies the corresponding native or ARIA state on the editing surface and documented state hook on the root. Styling SHALL NOT imply that a nested editor engine has enforced those states.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a consumer places classified attachment rows and a native submit button in their documented regions
- **THEN** each nested control retains its existing semantics and behavior contract
scenarios.id: forms/composer::Supporting regions compose existing controls::Attachments and submit action are provided
scenarios.name: Attachments and submit action are provided
scenarios.requirementContent: The attachments and actions regions SHALL accept existing SHLZ primitives or semantic consumer controls. Composer SHALL NOT own file selection, upload lifecycle, attachment removal, submit/send behavior, pending state, validation rules, persistence, or error recovery.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the consumer disables a command button
- **THEN** the control is unavailable to native activation and displays the disabled state
scenarios.id: forms/rich-text-toolbar::Command state is explicit and consumer-controlled::A command is unavailable
scenarios.name: A command is unavailable
scenarios.requirement: Command state is explicit and consumer-controlled
scenarios.requirementContent: Toggle commands SHALL expose their current state with `aria-pressed`; unavailable commands SHALL use native disabled semantics. The component SHALL style resting, hover, focus-visible, pressed, and disabled states without executing commands or deriving editor state.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the consumer sets a toggle command's `aria-pressed` value to `true`
- **THEN** the control exposes and visually presents its pressed state
scenarios.id: forms/rich-text-toolbar::Command state is explicit and consumer-controlled::A formatting mark is active
scenarios.name: A formatting mark is active
scenarios.requirement: Command state is explicit and consumer-controlled
scenarios.requirementContent: Toggle commands SHALL expose their current state with `aria-pressed`; unavailable commands SHALL use native disabled semantics. The component SHALL style resting, hover, focus-visible, pressed, and disabled states without executing commands or deriving editor state.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** command buttons are placed in the documented toolbar and group regions
- **THEN** assistive technology identifies the toolbar, each group, and the accessible name of every command
scenarios.id: forms/rich-text-toolbar::Rich Text Toolbar exposes semantic command controls::A consumer renders formatting commands
scenarios.name: A consumer renders formatting commands
scenarios.requirement: Rich Text Toolbar exposes semantic command controls
scenarios.requirementContent: The styles package SHALL support a `role="toolbar"` container with an accessible name. Command groups SHALL use `role="group"` with an accessible name. Commands SHALL be native buttons grouped by formatting purpose. Every icon-only command SHALL have an accessible name, and decorative icons SHALL remain hidden from assistive technology.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the toolbar is placed in a narrow container or content is enlarged
- **THEN** complete command groups wrap into additional rows and all controls remain visible and operable
scenarios.id: forms/rich-text-toolbar::Toolbar adapts to bounded width and content stress::Commands do not fit on one row
scenarios.name: Commands do not fit on one row
scenarios.requirement: Toolbar adapts to bounded width and content stress
scenarios.requirementContent: The toolbar SHALL allow command groups to wrap without clipping controls or introducing component-owned horizontal page overflow. Accessible names SHALL remain available when visible labels are omitted, and focus indicators SHALL remain unobscured at supported narrow widths.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the toolbar is rendered with semantic HTML and the styles package only
- **THEN** its controls remain reachable and activatable through native browser behavior while command effects remain consumer-owned
scenarios.id: forms/rich-text-toolbar::Toolbar interaction remains usable without a library controller::No behavior package is installed
scenarios.name: No behavior package is installed
scenarios.requirement: Toolbar interaction remains usable without a library controller
scenarios.requirementContent: The toolbar SHALL preserve native button keyboard and focus behavior and SHALL NOT require a JavaScript controller, roving tabindex, or editor implementation. The consumer SHALL own command execution, selection preservation, focus restoration, shortcuts, and synchronization with editor state.
